name: Difference of Sex Development of Gynecological Interest
aliases: Disorders of Sex Development (DSD) with Gynecological Manifestations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Statement on Management of Differences of Sex Development

criteria.description: Presence of ambiguous external genitalia at birth or during puberty
Identification of gonadal dysgenesis or atypical gonadal tissue on histology or imaging
Abnormal serum sex steroid hormone levels inconsistent with chromosomal sex
Detection of pathogenic variants in genes involved in sex development (e.g., SRY, NR5A1, AR)
Presence of Müllerian duct derivatives inconsistent with chromosomal sex

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ambiguous genitalia or gonadal dysgenesis plus abnormal hormonal profile or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including endocrinology, genetics, and gynecology.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes clitoromegaly, labioscrotal fusion, or hypospadias-like features
Failure to initiate menstruation by age 15
Streak gonads or underdeveloped gonadal tissue

common.notes: Enlarged clitoris beyond normal size for age
Lack of secondary sexual characteristics development
Inability to conceive due to gonadal or anatomical abnormalities

common.symptomName: Elevated luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)
common.notes: Indicative of gonadal failure or dysgenesis

occasional.notes: Excessive hair growth in androgen-sensitive areas
Presence of uterus or fallopian tubes inconsistent with chromosomal sex
Emotional or psychological difficulties related to gender identity or body image
Development of cystic structures in gonadal tissue

rare.notes: Malignant tumor risk in dysgenetic gonads
Due to excess mineralocorticoid production in some enzyme deficiencies
searchTerms: high blood pressure from adrenal enlargement
hypertension due to adrenal gland problem
blood pressure raised by adrenal hyperplasia

rare.notes: Life-threatening acute adrenal insufficiency in enzyme defects

laboratory: Abnormal serum sex steroid hormone levels (e.g., testosterone, estradiol)
Electrolyte imbalances in enzyme deficiencies (e.g., 21-hydroxylase deficiency)
imaging: Pelvic ultrasound showing absent or hypoplastic uterus or ovaries
MRI of pelvis for gonadal tissue characterization
Genitography to assess internal reproductive anatomy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in SRY, NR5A1, AR, CYP21A2, and other sex development genes
Karyotype analysis showing sex chromosome anomalies (e.g., 46,XY or 46,XX mosaicism)
other: Histopathology of gonadal tissue revealing dysgenesis or tumor
Psychological evaluation for gender identity and counseling needs

distinguishingFeatures: Normal or elevated testosterone with androgen receptor mutations
Enzyme deficiency causing cortisol synthesis impairment

redFlags: Ambiguous genitalia at birth requiring urgent evaluation
Rapid virilization during infancy or puberty
Signs of adrenal crisis such as vomiting, dehydration, and hypotension
references: Hughes IA, et al. Consensus statement on management of differences of sex development. Nat Rev Endocrinol. 2006.
Lee PA, et al. Global Disorders of Sex Development Update since 2006: Perceptions, Approach and Care. Horm Res Paediatr. 2016.
